sections.h2: Why a Frankfort house can have two tax bills
sections.html:
The City of Frankfort taxes inside its limits on top of the county. Everyone in Franklin County gets a county bill from the Franklin County Sheriff, and a house in Frankfort also gets a city bill from the Finance Office, which collects for Frankfort Independent Schools too.

The Franklin County PVA sets the values for both bills. It is at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, Frankfort, with a fax at (502) 226-5495 and a phone at (502) 875-8780, open weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30. The sheriff has moved to the Public Safety Complex at 974 River Bend Road and answers at (502) 875-8740. The sheriff's website offers a tax bill search with card payment, and the front door has a secure drop box under camera watch.

Frankfort uses the PVA's figure, which is 100 percent of fair market value as of each January 1. Questions about a value, an exemption or a mailing address belong with the PVA, not the city.

The city does not copy the state schedule. County bills follow KRS 134.015, while Frankfort publishes its own dates, so a deadline that works for one bill can already be past for the other.

Owners with an escrow account should pass the bill to the servicer, because a lender cannot pay a bill it never received. Missing the city date is the easy mistake here: the county bill's November 1 credit and the city's November 30 credit are different so check which date applies to which bill. City commissioners vote the city rate each year on the finance director's advice, and Frankfort Independent Schools sets the old city school rate.

sections.h2: Franklin County housing and the buyer pool
sections.html:
Franklin County is the seat of state government and is more urban than most of Kentucky. Two school systems share the area. Franklin County Public Schools covers nearly all of it, including most of Frankfort, while Frankfort Independent Schools covers downtown, South Frankfort around the Capitol, and Bellepoint. Population is 52,649. Sellers should expect buyers to ask about both bills, since the city charge is extra for any house inside the limits.

The typical house value is $216,600. Owners live in 64.5 percent of homes, which leaves a large rental share. There are 24,404 housing units, median gross rent is $967, and 96 permits for new homes were issued in 2025. With the state workforce nearby, sellers in Frankfort draw from a deeper buyer pool than most Kentucky counties offer, and tax bills run larger in dollars. A seller carrying a tax balance should collect payoff figures from both billing offices before picking a closing date.

Meet the PVA first, because the state will not take an appeal from an owner who skipped the conference. The roll is posted for 13 days beginning in the first week of May, and the PVA has to advertise that period in the county's largest newspaper.

Next, file at the county clerk's office by the end of the following business day. A local board of assessment appeals then hears cases roughly four or five weeks later. It listens only to evidence offered with you and the PVA both present, so bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal, repair estimates or insurance records. You may audio-record the hearing, and the board owes you a written explanation of any change. If bills have already printed when the board raises a value, a supplemental bill makes up the gap.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you list
sections.html:
A Frankfort sale involves two tax accounts, so a short checklist saves time.

  • Find out whether the house is inside the city limits. If it is, expect a county bill and a city bill, and ask whether the city bill also carries the school charge.
  • Call the sheriff at (502) 875-8740 and, for a city address, the Finance Office at (502) 875-8500. Ask what is owed and what has already been paid this year.
  • Keep the paid receipts. The buyer's title company will ask for both.
  • If you claim the homestead exemption, tell the PVA at (502) 875-8780 once the sale is final so the exemption does not stay attached to your old address.

Bring the deed or a recent bill to any of these offices. It carries the parcel details staff need to pull your account without delay.

Seniors and totally disabled owners qualify, as long as the house is their home. The state exemption is $49,100 in 2025 and 2026, deducted from assessed value before tax is calculated.

File with the Franklin County PVA. Ask that office how the January 1 ownership date applies if you buy or sell partway through a year, and tell it about any sale so the exemption comes off the old address.

sections.h2: Selling with unpaid Franklin County taxes
sections.html:
The tax follows the parcel to the closing table. KRS 134.015 treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a delinquency lien survives a change of ownership.

Open bills pass from the sheriff to the county clerk on April 15. From then on 1 percent interest accrues every month, the clerk takes a 10 percent commission, and a county attorney commission of 20 percent applies after the first notice goes out. The county attorney mails notices before any sale, which must fall between 90 and 135 days after the transfer.

  • Ask the sheriff for a payoff at (502) 875-8740, and the city Finance Office at (502) 875-8500 if the house is in Frankfort.
  • Have the title company pay both bills from your proceeds so the policy issues clean.
  • A buyer that purchases as-is and closes quickly can take over a house with arrears and repairs without a listing period.

Because the county and the city keep separate records, a change of address filed with one does not reach the other. After closing, tell the PVA the buyer's name and mailing address, and tell the city Finance Office too if the house is inside Frankfort. That way the next county and city bills reach the new owner instead of coming back to you.

faqs.q: Do Frankfort homeowners pay the city and the county?
faqs.a: Yes. They receive a county bill collected by the sheriff and a city bill collected by the Finance Office, which also collects for Frankfort Independent Schools.

faqs.q: Where is the Franklin County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 974 River Bend Road, Frankfort, KY 40601, and the phone is (502) 875-8740. Bills can also be searched and paid on the sheriff's website.

faqs.q: Where is the Franklin County PVA?
faqs.a: It is at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, Frankfort, KY 40601. The phone is (502) 875-8780, and weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:30.

faqs.q: How big is the Franklin County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Seniors and totally disabled owners apply through the PVA, and the amount is subtracted from the assessed value.

faqs.q: How soon after April 15 can Franklin County hold a tax sale?
faqs.a: The sale must fall between 90 and 135 days after the sheriff transfers the bills to the clerk, and the county attorney mails notices beforehand.
